addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

Experience ultra-low-latency inference with **GLM-5** and **DeepSeek-V3.2**. The v0.1.3 release introduces full support for the latest GLM-5 model, achieving up to 500 tokens/s on GLM-5-FP8 and up to 600 tokens/s on DeepSeek-V3.2. 37 38 - 🚀 **2026-01-26 · [v0.1.2-alpha.1](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.2-alpha.1)**. **Multi-Token Prediction (MTP)** is now available in TileRT! With mtp=3, we achieve decoding rates of up to **590 tokens/s** under synthetic workloads. 39 40 - ⚡ **2025-12-23 · [v0.1.1](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.1)**. Achieved ~**35% further reduction** (3 ~ 4x speedup over baseline) in end-to-end token generation latency on a single node with **8× NVIDIA B200**. 41 42 - 🚀 **2025-11-20 · [v0.1.0-alpha.1](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.1)**. Initial public release for **DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp**, targeting **ultra-low-latency** inference. Available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tilert) and [HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/Tile-AI/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp-TileRT). 43 44
45 46 ______________________________________________________________________ 47 48 49 50 **TileRT** is a project designed to serve large language models (LLMs) in ultra-low-latency scenarios. Its goal is to push the latency limits of LLMs without compromising model size or quality—enabling models with hundreds of billions of parameters to achieve millisecond-level time per output token (TPOT). 51 52 Unlike traditional inference systems optimized for high-throughput batch processing, TileRT prioritizes **responsiveness**, which is critical for applications such as high-frequency trading, interactive AI, real-time decision-making, long-running agents, and AI-assisted coding, where the latency of individual requests matters most. 53 54 To achieve this, TileRT introduces a **tile-level runtime engine**. Leveraging a compiler-driven approach, LLM operators are decomposed into fine-grained tile-level tasks, while the runtime dynamically reschedules computation, I/O, and communication across multiple devices in a highly overlapped manner. This design minimizes idle time and improves hardware utilization. 55 56 The project is actively evolving, and the underlying compiler techniques will be gradually shared with the community as they are integrated into **TileLang** and **TileScale**. 57 58

59 60
61 GLM-5.1-FP8 token generation speed on 8× NVIDIA B200 with TileRT v0.1.5. Output length 1K, input length 1K–192K. Bars compare TileRT without MTP, with MTP at average acceptance length 3.2, and the peak under best-case MTP acceptance (4.0). 62

63 64 ______________________________________________________________________ 65 66 ## Installation 67 68 > \[!IMPORTANT\] 69 > TileRT v0.1.5 is distributed as a **pre-built binary wheel**. The wheel is linked against the exact ABI of the versions listed below. Other combinations of Python, CUDA, or PyTorch versions are **untested and not guaranteed to work** — please reproduce this environment for a supported setup. 70 71 ### Build environment of the v0.1.5 wheel 72 73 The official `tilert==0.1.5.post1` wheel on PyPI was compiled against the following stack. Treat these as **hard requirements**, not lower bounds. 74 75 | Component | Pinned version | 76 | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | 77 | GPU | 8× NVIDIA **B200** | 78 | NVIDIA driver | Supports **CUDA 13.2** runtime | 79 | Operating System | Linux **x86_64**, glibc **≥ 2.28** (manylinux_2_28) | 80 | Python | **3.12** | 81 | PyTorch | **`torch==2.11.0+cu130`** | 82 | `transformers` | **`4.46.3`** | 83 | `tokenizers` | **`0.20.3`** | 84 85 ### Recommended: pre-built Docker image 86 87 The pinned build environment above is preinstalled in our official image 88 — this is the **recommended way to run v0.1.5** and avoids any version 89 drift on the host. The image is mirrored to two registries; pull from 90 whichever is reachable: 91 92 ```bash 93 # GitHub Container Registry 94 docker pull ghcr.io/tile-ai/tilert:cu132-latest 95 96 # Docker Hub 97 docker pull tileai/tilert:cu132-latest 98 ``` 99 100 Launch a container with all 8 B200 GPUs attached, then install the 101 wheel inside: 102 103 ```bash 104 docker run --rm -it --gpus all --ipc=host \ 105 -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace \ 106 ghcr.io/tile-ai/tilert:cu132-latest 107 108 # Inside the container — install from PyPI: 109 pip install tilert==0.1.5.post1 110 111 # Or pin the exact wheel from the GitHub Release page directly 112 # (same artifact, useful when PyPI is unreachable): 113 pip install https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/download/v0.1.5/tilert-0.1.5.post1-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl 114 ``` 115 116 Verify the install: 117 118 ```bash 119 python -c "import tilert, torch; print('tilert', tilert.__version__, '/ torch', torch.__version__, '/ cuda', torch.version.cuda)" 120 # Expected: tilert 0.1.5.post1 / torch 2.11.0+cu130 / cuda 13.0 121 ``` 122 123 Proceed to [Getting Started](#getting-started) to download and convert model weights. 124 125 ## Getting Started 126 127 ### Step 1: Download Official Model Weights 128 129 Starting from release v0.1.3, TileRT no longer requires downloading pre-converted weights from Hugging Face. Instead, you can download the official model weights directly from the model's source (e.g., Hugging Face), and then convert them using the weight converter script included with the latest TileRT release. 130 131 ### Step 2: Shard Weights with `weight_converter` 132 133 The converter ships inside the `tilert` wheel. It rewrites the official HF 134 checkpoint into TileRT's per-device layout — 8 shards, one per B200, with 135 keys suffixed `*_dev_{0..7}` and a fresh `model.safetensors.index.json`. 136 The runtime loads these shards directly; the original checkpoint is no 137 longer needed after conversion. 138 139 For **DeepSeek-V3.2**: 140 141 ```bash 142 python -m tilert.models.preprocess.weight_converter \ 143 --model_type deepseek-v32 \ 144 --model_dir "/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2" \ 145 --save_dir "/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT" 146 ``` 147 148 For **GLM-5/5.1**: 149 150 ```bash 151 python -m tilert.models.preprocess.weight_converter \ 152 --model_type glm-5 \ 153 --model_dir "/path/to/GLM-5-FP8" \ 154 --save_dir "/path/to/GLM-5-FP8-TileRT" 155 ``` 156 157 `--model_dir` is the directory of the downloaded HF checkpoint; 158 `--save_dir` is where the sharded TileRT-format weights will land. 159 160 ### Step 3: Register the Sharded Weights Path 161 162 Either pass `--model-weights-dir ` on every `tilert.generate` 163 invocation, or register the path once in `~/.tilert/config.toml` so the 164 CLI picks it up automatically: 165 166 ```toml 167 [weights] 168 deepseek_v3_2 = "/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT" 169 glm5 = "/path/to/GLM-5-FP8-TileRT" 170 ``` 171 172 ### Running the Generation Example 173 174 The simplest entry point is the bundled CLI. Pick `--model deepseek_v3_2` 175 or `--model glm5`; weights resolve from `~/.tilert/config.toml` or from 176 an explicit `--model-weights-dir`: 177 178 ```bash 179 python -m tilert.generate --model deepseek_v3_2 --max-new-tokens 1000 180 ``` 181 182 > \[!NOTE\] 183 > v0.1.5 ships **two independent backend libraries** (`libtilert_dsv32.so` 184 > and `libtilert_glm5.so`) and loads exactly one per Python process via 185 > `tilert.load_backend(model_type)`. Run DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 in 186 > separate processes — they cannot coexist in a single interpreter. 187 188 To drive generation programmatically, load the backend first, then build 189 the matching generator: 190 191 ```python 192 import tilert 193 from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.generator import DSAv32Generator 194 from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.model_args import ModelArgs 195 196 tilert.load_backend("deepseek_v3_2") 197 198 generator = DSAv32Generator( 199 model_args=ModelArgs(), 200 max_new_tokens=1000, 201 model_weights_dir="/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT", 202 with_mtp=False, 203 ) 204 generator.from_pretrained() 205 206 prompt = ( 207 "Tell me three jokes:\n\n" 208 "1. A dad joke,\n" 209 "2. A programmer joke,\n" 210 "3. A joke that only makes sense if you've ever tried " 211 "to train a large language model.\n" 212 "Keep each joke under 15 words." 213 ) 214 215 print("Prompt:", prompt) 216 print("Completion:") 217 completion = generator.generate(prompt) 218 ``` 219 220 (For **GLM-5**, swap in `tilert.load_backend("glm5")` and 221 `from tilert.models.glm_5.generator import GLM5Generator` with 222 `ModelArgsGLM5`.) 223 224 For example, TileRT may generate: 225 226
227 Sample output (click to expand) 228 229 ```text 230 1. I'm afraid for the calendar. Its days are numbered. 231 2. There are only 10 kinds of people: those who understand binary and those who don't. 232 3. My model's loss is low, but its answers are still nonsense. Overfitting. 233 ``` 234 235
236 237 This example demonstrates basic single-step autoregressive generation using the precompiled model. 238 239 ### Running the Generation Example with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) 240 241 TileRT also supports Multi-Token Prediction (MTP), which allows the model to generate multiple tokens per forward pass and reduces sequential decoding depth. Enable it from the CLI with `--with-mtp`: 242 243 ```bash 244 python -m tilert.generate --model deepseek_v3_2 --with-mtp --max-new-tokens 1000 245 ``` 246 247 Or programmatically, pass `with_mtp=True` to the generator: 248 249 ```python 250 import tilert 251 from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.generator import DSAv32Generator 252 from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.model_args import ModelArgs 253 254 tilert.load_backend("deepseek_v3_2") 255 256 generator = DSAv32Generator( 257 model_args=ModelArgs(), 258 max_new_tokens=1000, 259 model_weights_dir="/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT", 260 with_mtp=True, 261 ) 262 generator.from_pretrained() 263 prompt = "Tell me 10 jokes, keep them all under 100 words." 264 265 print("Prompt:", prompt) 266 print("Completion:") 267 completion = generator.generate(prompt) 268 ``` 269 270 When MTP is enabled, TileRT may report statistics similar to the following during generation: 271 272 ```text 273 Accepted length: mean=2.77, min=1, max=4 274 ``` 275 276 This indicates that, on average, multiple tokens are accepted per decoding step under MTP. 277 278
279 Sample output (click to expand) 280 281 ```text 282 Of course! Here are 10 short jokes for you. 283 284 1. I told my wife she was drawing her eyebrows too high. She looked surprised. 285 286 2. I invented a new word: Plagiarism. 287 288 3. Why don't scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything. 289 290 4. I'm reading a book on anti-gravity. It's impossible to put down. 291 292 5. What's the best thing about Switzerland? I don't know, but the flag is a big plus. 293 294 6. I told my computer I needed a break, and now it won't stop sending me vacation ads. 295 296 7. Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field. 297 298 8. What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta. 299 300 9. I told my suitcase there's no vacation, and now it has a lot of baggage. 301 302 10. Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts. 303 ``` 304 305
306 307 This example highlights how MTP enables TileRT to efficiently generate longer outputs by accepting multiple tokens per decoding step, while preserving the same Python API interface. 308 309 For the full list of CLI flags (sampling, batching, benchmark modes, …), run `python -m tilert.generate --help`. 310 311 ## Disaggregated Serving: vLLM Prefill + TileRT Decode 312 313 TileRT can run as the **decode engine behind a vLLM prefill**, integrated through vLLM's V1 `KVConnector` interface. The connector, decode server, and router all ship inside the `tilert` wheel under `tilert.pd_vllm` — no vLLM fork or patch is needed (the connector loads via vLLM's standard `kv_connector_module_path`). Latency-critical requests are routed to the TileRT decode pool; other traffic can stay on native vLLM decode. 314 315 **Prerequisites** 316 317 - Convert the model weights for TileRT decode (see [Step 2](#step-2-shard-weights-with-weight_converter)). 318 - On the **prefill** node, a vLLM build with V1 disaggregation and support for the GLM-5/5.1 / DeepSeek-V3.2 (DSA) model and the `fp8_ds_mla` KV-cache dtype. Install `tilert` in the same environment so the connector plugin is importable. 319 - **The KV-cache dtype must match on both ends.** These examples use fp8: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` on the vLLM prefill and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` on the TileRT decode (a mismatch is rejected at the connector handshake). 320 - The examples use the **NIXL** transfer engine. On multi-NIC hosts, pin NIXL to the RDMA NICs via `UCX_NET_DEVICES` (otherwise UCX may pick the wrong interface). Mooncake is also supported (`--transport mooncake` on the decode, `"tilert_transport": "mooncake"` on the prefill). 321 322 Commands below use GLM-5/5.1. For DeepSeek-V3.2, use `--model deepseek_v3_2`, the DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT weights, and `--parser none`. 323 324 ### Topology A: vLLM prefill → TileRT decode 325 326 Three processes — a TileRT decode server, a stock vLLM prefill, and an OpenAI-compatible router: 327 328 ```bash 329 # 1) TileRT decode node 330 python -m tilert.pd_vllm.decode_server \ 331 --engine tilert --model glm5 \ 332 --model-weights-dir /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8-TileRT \ 333 --with-mtp --max-seq-len 202752 \ 334 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --transport nixl \ 335 --ctrl-port 5556 --http-port 5557 336 337 # 2) vLLM prefill (stock vLLM; the TileRT connector loads as a plugin). 338 # The MTP speculative config is required: the prefill populates the 339 # draft-layer KV that decode-side speculation resumes from. 340 export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_1:1,mlx5_2:1,... # pin NIXL to the RDMA NICs (multi-NIC hosts) 341 vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ 342 --served-model-name glm5 --port 8000 \ 343 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code \ 344 --return-tokens-as-token-ids --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \ 345 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ 346 --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \ 347 --kv-transfer-config '{ 348 "kv_connector": "TileRTConnector", 349 "kv_connector_module_path": "tilert.pd_vllm.prefill_connector", 350 "kv_role": "kv_producer", 351 "kv_connector_extra_config": { 352 "tilert_host": "", "tilert_ctrl_port": 5556, 353 "tilert_model": "glm5", "tilert_max_seq_len": 202752, 354 "tilert_transport": "nixl"}}' 355 356 # 3) Router — OpenAI-compatible ingress for the TileRT pool 357 python -m tilert.pd_vllm.pd_router \ 358 --vllm-url http://:8000 \ 359 --decode :5556:5557 \ 360 --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ 361 --parser glm47 --port 23333 362 ``` 363 364 Send OpenAI requests to `http://:23333/v1/chat/completions`. The router runs the prefill on vLLM (first token), hands the attention state to the TileRT decode node over RDMA, and streams the completion back. 365 366 ### Topology B: shared prefill → TileRT decode **and** native vLLM decode 367 368 One prefill pool feeds two decode pools side by side, composed under vLLM's `MultiConnector`. Each request is claimed by exactly one connector — the TileRT connector claims requests marked with `tilert_host`, and vLLM's native connector handles the rest — so latency-critical traffic goes to TileRT while general traffic stays on native vLLM decode, behind the same OpenAI surface. 369 370 ```bash 371 # 1) TileRT decode node (identical to Topology A) 372 python -m tilert.pd_vllm.decode_server --engine tilert --model glm5 \ 373 --model-weights-dir /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8-TileRT --with-mtp \ 374 --max-seq-len 202752 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --transport nixl \ 375 --ctrl-port 5556 --http-port 5557 376 377 # 2) Native vLLM decode node — vLLM's standard disaggregation (NixlConnector consumer) 378 export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_1:1,mlx5_2:1,... 379 vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 --served-model-name glm5 --port 8001 \ 380 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code \ 381 --return-tokens-as-token-ids --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ 382 --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \ 383 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}' 384 385 # 4a) TileRT router — latency-critical traffic → TileRT pool 405 python -m tilert.pd_vllm.pd_router --vllm-url http://:8000 \ 406 --decode :5556:5557 --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ 407 --parser glm47 --port 23333 408 409 # TileRT: Tile-Based Runtime for
Ultra-Low-Latency LLM Inference

Overview · Generation · MTP Generation · Installation · News

______________________________________________________________________ ## 📰 News - 🔀 **2026-07-14 · [v0.1.5](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.5) Released**. Introduce [**PD (prefill–decode) disaggregation**](https://www.tilert.ai/blog/tilert-vllm-disaggregation.html) — vLLM prefill + TileRT decode, behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Supported on GLM-5/5.1 and DeepSeek-V3.2. - 💥 **2026-06-08 · [Breaking 1000 TPS on a 1T Model](https://www.tilert.ai/blog/breaking-1000-tps.html)**. In collaboration with [Xiaomi MiMo](https://mimo.xiaomi.com/blog/mimo-tilert-1000tps), TileRT pushes [**MiMo-V2.5-Pro-UltraSpeed**](https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/docs/en-US/model-intro/mimo-v2.5-pro-ultraspeed) past **1000 tokens/s** on a **1-trillion-parameter** model through extreme model–system co-design — a first without custom silicon, all on a single 8-GPU node. - 🚀 **2026-06-01 · [v0.1.4](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.4) Released**. A major performance upgrade for both DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5, with model quality unchanged. See the benchmark charts for details. - 🏭 **2026-05-22 · [TileRT in Production](https://www.tilert.ai/blog/speed-as-the-next-scaling-law-zh.html)**. [**GLM-5.1-highspeed**](https://docs.bigmodel.cn/cn/guide/models/text/glm-5.1-highspeed) is now live on Z.ai, powered by TileRT — from experimental prototype to real production.
Key Milestones - :fire: **2026-02-14 · [Try the Online Demo](https://www.tilert.ai/)**. Our online demo is now live! Experience ultra-low-latency inference with **GLM-5** and **DeepSeek-V3.2**. [Try it now !](https://www.tilert.ai) - 🎉 **2026-02-14 · [v0.1.3](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.3) Released**. The v0.1.3 release introduces full support for the latest GLM-5 model, achieving up to 500 tokens/s on GLM-5-FP8 and up to 600 tokens/s on DeepSeek-V3.2. - 🚀 **2026-01-26 · [v0.1.2-alpha.1](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.2-alpha.1)**. **Multi-Token Prediction (MTP)** is now available in TileRT! With mtp=3, we achieve decoding rates of up to **590 tokens/s** under synthetic workloads. - ⚡ **2025-12-23 · [v0.1.1](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.1)**. Achieved ~**35% further reduction** (3 ~ 4x speedup over baseline) in end-to-end token generation latency on a single node with **8× NVIDIA B200**. - 🚀 **2025-11-20 · [v0.1.0-alpha.1](https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.1)**. Initial public release for **DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp**, targeting **ultra-low-latency** inference. Available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tilert) and [HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/Tile-AI/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp-TileRT).
______________________________________________________________________ **TileRT** is a project designed to serve large language models (LLMs) in ultra-low-latency scenarios. Its goal is to push the latency limits of LLMs without compromising model size or quality—enabling models with hundreds of billions of parameters to achieve millisecond-level time per output token (TPOT). Unlike traditional inference systems optimized for high-throughput batch processing, TileRT prioritizes **responsiveness**, which is critical for applications such as high-frequency trading, interactive AI, real-time decision-making, long-running agents, and AI-assisted coding, where the latency of individual requests matters most. To achieve this, TileRT introduces a **tile-level runtime engine**. Leveraging a compiler-driven approach, LLM operators are decomposed into fine-grained tile-level tasks, while the runtime dynamically reschedules computation, I/O, and communication across multiple devices in a highly overlapped manner. This design minimizes idle time and improves hardware utilization. The project is actively evolving, and the underlying compiler techniques will be gradually shared with the community as they are integrated into **TileLang** and **TileScale**.


GLM-5.1-FP8 token generation speed on 8× NVIDIA B200 with TileRT v0.1.5. Output length 1K, input length 1K–192K. Bars compare TileRT without MTP, with MTP at average acceptance length 3.2, and the peak under best-case MTP acceptance (4.0).

______________________________________________________________________ ## Installation > \[!IMPORTANT\] > TileRT v0.1.5 is distributed as a **pre-built binary wheel**. The wheel is linked against the exact ABI of the versions listed below. Other combinations of Python, CUDA, or PyTorch versions are **untested and not guaranteed to work** — please reproduce this environment for a supported setup. ### Build environment of the v0.1.5 wheel The official `tilert==0.1.5.post1` wheel on PyPI was compiled against the following stack. Treat these as **hard requirements**, not lower bounds. | Component | Pinned version | | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | GPU | 8× NVIDIA **B200** | | NVIDIA driver | Supports **CUDA 13.2** runtime | | Operating System | Linux **x86_64**, glibc **≥ 2.28** (manylinux_2_28) | | Python | **3.12** | | PyTorch | **`torch==2.11.0+cu130`** | | `transformers` | **`4.46.3`** | | `tokenizers` | **`0.20.3`** | ### Recommended: pre-built Docker image The pinned build environment above is preinstalled in our official image — this is the **recommended way to run v0.1.5** and avoids any version drift on the host. The image is mirrored to two registries; pull from whichever is reachable: ```bash # GitHub Container Registry docker pull ghcr.io/tile-ai/tilert:cu132-latest # Docker Hub docker pull tileai/tilert:cu132-latest ``` Launch a container with all 8 B200 GPUs attached, then install the wheel inside: ```bash docker run --rm -it --gpus all --ipc=host \ -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace \ ghcr.io/tile-ai/tilert:cu132-latest # Inside the container — install from PyPI: pip install tilert==0.1.5.post1 # Or pin the exact wheel from the GitHub Release page directly # (same artifact, useful when PyPI is unreachable): pip install https://github.com/tile-ai/TileRT/releases/download/v0.1.5/tilert-0.1.5.post1-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl ``` Verify the install: ```bash python -c "import tilert, torch; print('tilert', tilert.__version__, '/ torch', torch.__version__, '/ cuda', torch.version.cuda)" # Expected: tilert 0.1.5.post1 / torch 2.11.0+cu130 / cuda 13.0 ``` Proceed to [Getting Started](#getting-started) to download and convert model weights. ## Getting Started ### Step 1: Download Official Model Weights Starting from release v0.1.3, TileRT no longer requires downloading pre-converted weights from Hugging Face. Instead, you can download the official model weights directly from the model's source (e.g., Hugging Face), and then convert them using the weight converter script included with the latest TileRT release. ### Step 2: Shard Weights with `weight_converter` The converter ships inside the `tilert` wheel. It rewrites the official HF checkpoint into TileRT's per-device layout — 8 shards, one per B200, with keys suffixed `*_dev_{0..7}` and a fresh `model.safetensors.index.json`. The runtime loads these shards directly; the original checkpoint is no longer needed after conversion. For **DeepSeek-V3.2**: ```bash python -m tilert.models.preprocess.weight_converter \ --model_type deepseek-v32 \ --model_dir "/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2" \ --save_dir "/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT" ``` For **GLM-5/5.1**: ```bash python -m tilert.models.preprocess.weight_converter \ --model_type glm-5 \ --model_dir "/path/to/GLM-5-FP8" \ --save_dir "/path/to/GLM-5-FP8-TileRT" ``` `--model_dir` is the directory of the downloaded HF checkpoint; `--save_dir` is where the sharded TileRT-format weights will land. ### Step 3: Register the Sharded Weights Path Either pass `--model-weights-dir ` on every `tilert.generate` invocation, or register the path once in `~/.tilert/config.toml` so the CLI picks it up automatically: ```toml [weights] deepseek_v3_2 = "/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT" glm5 = "/path/to/GLM-5-FP8-TileRT" ``` ### Running the Generation Example The simplest entry point is the bundled CLI. Pick `--model deepseek_v3_2` or `--model glm5`; weights resolve from `~/.tilert/config.toml` or from an explicit `--model-weights-dir`: ```bash python -m tilert.generate --model deepseek_v3_2 --max-new-tokens 1000 ``` > \[!NOTE\] > v0.1.5 ships **two independent backend libraries** (`libtilert_dsv32.so` > and `libtilert_glm5.so`) and loads exactly one per Python process via > `tilert.load_backend(model_type)`. Run DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 in > separate processes — they cannot coexist in a single interpreter. To drive generation programmatically, load the backend first, then build the matching generator: ```python import tilert from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.generator import DSAv32Generator from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.model_args import ModelArgs tilert.load_backend("deepseek_v3_2") generator = DSAv32Generator( model_args=ModelArgs(), max_new_tokens=1000, model_weights_dir="/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT", with_mtp=False, ) generator.from_pretrained() prompt = ( "Tell me three jokes:\n\n" "1. A dad joke,\n" "2. A programmer joke,\n" "3. A joke that only makes sense if you've ever tried " "to train a large language model.\n" "Keep each joke under 15 words." ) print("Prompt:", prompt) print("Completion:") completion = generator.generate(prompt) ``` (For **GLM-5**, swap in `tilert.load_backend("glm5")` and `from tilert.models.glm_5.generator import GLM5Generator` with `ModelArgsGLM5`.) For example, TileRT may generate:
Sample output (click to expand) ```text 1. I'm afraid for the calendar. Its days are numbered. 2. There are only 10 kinds of people: those who understand binary and those who don't. 3. My model's loss is low, but its answers are still nonsense. Overfitting. ```
This example demonstrates basic single-step autoregressive generation using the precompiled model. ### Running the Generation Example with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) TileRT also supports Multi-Token Prediction (MTP), which allows the model to generate multiple tokens per forward pass and reduces sequential decoding depth. Enable it from the CLI with `--with-mtp`: ```bash python -m tilert.generate --model deepseek_v3_2 --with-mtp --max-new-tokens 1000 ``` Or programmatically, pass `with_mtp=True` to the generator: ```python import tilert from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.generator import DSAv32Generator from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.model_args import ModelArgs tilert.load_backend("deepseek_v3_2") generator = DSAv32Generator( model_args=ModelArgs(), max_new_tokens=1000, model_weights_dir="/path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT", with_mtp=True, ) generator.from_pretrained() prompt = "Tell me 10 jokes, keep them all under 100 words." print("Prompt:", prompt) print("Completion:") completion = generator.generate(prompt) ``` When MTP is enabled, TileRT may report statistics similar to the following during generation: ```text Accepted length: mean=2.77, min=1, max=4 ``` This indicates that, on average, multiple tokens are accepted per decoding step under MTP.
Sample output (click to expand) ```text Of course! Here are 10 short jokes for you. 1. I told my wife she was drawing her eyebrows too high. She looked surprised. 2. I invented a new word: Plagiarism. 3. Why don't scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything. 4. I'm reading a book on anti-gravity. It's impossible to put down. 5. What's the best thing about Switzerland? I don't know, but the flag is a big plus. 6. I told my computer I needed a break, and now it won't stop sending me vacation ads. 7. Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field. 8. What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta. 9. I told my suitcase there's no vacation, and now it has a lot of baggage. 10. Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts. ```
This example highlights how MTP enables TileRT to efficiently generate longer outputs by accepting multiple tokens per decoding step, while preserving the same Python API interface. For the full list of CLI flags (sampling, batching, benchmark modes, …), run `python -m tilert.generate --help`. ## Disaggregated Serving: vLLM Prefill + TileRT Decode TileRT can run as the **decode engine behind a vLLM prefill**, integrated through vLLM's V1 `KVConnector` interface. The connector, decode server, and router all ship inside the `tilert` wheel under `tilert.pd_vllm` — no vLLM fork or patch is needed (the connector loads via vLLM's standard `kv_connector_module_path`). Latency-critical requests are routed to the TileRT decode pool; other traffic can stay on native vLLM decode. **Prerequisites** - Convert the model weights for TileRT decode (see [Step 2](#step-2-shard-weights-with-weight_converter)). - On the **prefill** node, a vLLM build with V1 disaggregation and support for the GLM-5/5.1 / DeepSeek-V3.2 (DSA) model and the `fp8_ds_mla` KV-cache dtype. Install `tilert` in the same environment so the connector plugin is importable. - **The KV-cache dtype must match on both ends.** These examples use fp8: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` on the vLLM prefill and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` on the TileRT decode (a mismatch is rejected at the connector handshake). - The examples use the **NIXL** transfer engine. On multi-NIC hosts, pin NIXL to the RDMA NICs via `UCX_NET_DEVICES` (otherwise UCX may pick the wrong interface). Mooncake is also supported (`--transport mooncake` on the decode, `"tilert_transport": "mooncake"` on the prefill). Commands below use GLM-5/5.1. For DeepSeek-V3.2, use `--model deepseek_v3_2`, the DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT weights, and `--parser none`. ### Topology A: vLLM prefill → TileRT decode Three processes — a TileRT decode server, a stock vLLM prefill, and an OpenAI-compatible router: ```bash # 1) TileRT decode node python -m tilert.pd_vllm.decode_server \ --engine tilert --model glm5 \ --model-weights-dir /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8-TileRT \ --with-mtp --max-seq-len 202752 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --transport nixl \ --ctrl-port 5556 --http-port 5557 # 2) vLLM prefill (stock vLLM; the TileRT connector loads as a plugin). # The MTP speculative config is required: the prefill populates the # draft-layer KV that decode-side speculation resumes from. export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_1:1,mlx5_2:1,... # pin NIXL to the RDMA NICs (multi-NIC hosts) vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ --served-model-name glm5 --port 8000 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code \ --return-tokens-as-token-ids --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector": "TileRTConnector", "kv_connector_module_path": "tilert.pd_vllm.prefill_connector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "tilert_host": "", "tilert_ctrl_port": 5556, "tilert_model": "glm5", "tilert_max_seq_len": 202752, "tilert_transport": "nixl"}}' # 3) Router — OpenAI-compatible ingress for the TileRT pool python -m tilert.pd_vllm.pd_router \ --vllm-url http://:8000 \ --decode :5556:5557 \ --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ --parser glm47 --port 23333 ``` Send OpenAI requests to `http://:23333/v1/chat/completions`. The router runs the prefill on vLLM (first token), hands the attention state to the TileRT decode node over RDMA, and streams the completion back. ### Topology B: shared prefill → TileRT decode **and** native vLLM decode One prefill pool feeds two decode pools side by side, composed under vLLM's `MultiConnector`. Each request is claimed by exactly one connector — the TileRT connector claims requests marked with `tilert_host`, and vLLM's native connector handles the rest — so latency-critical traffic goes to TileRT while general traffic stays on native vLLM decode, behind the same OpenAI surface. ```bash # 1) TileRT decode node (identical to Topology A) python -m tilert.pd_vllm.decode_server --engine tilert --model glm5 \ --model-weights-dir /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8-TileRT --with-mtp \ --max-seq-len 202752 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --transport nixl \ --ctrl-port 5556 --http-port 5557 # 2) Native vLLM decode node — vLLM's standard disaggregation (NixlConnector consumer) export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_1:1,mlx5_2:1,... vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 --served-model-name glm5 --port 8001 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code \ --return-tokens-as-token-ids --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer"}' # 3) Shared vLLM prefill — MultiConnector[ NixlConnector + TileRTConnector ] export UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_1:1,mlx5_2:1,... vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 --served-model-name glm5 --port 8000 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code \ --return-tokens-as-token-ids --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"connectors": [ {"kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer"}, {"kv_connector": "TileRTConnector", "kv_connector_module_path": "tilert.pd_vllm.prefill_connector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "tilert_host": "", "tilert_ctrl_port": 5556, "tilert_model": "glm5", "tilert_max_seq_len": 202752, "tilert_transport": "nixl"}}]}}' # 4a) TileRT router — latency-critical traffic → TileRT pool python -m tilert.pd_vllm.pd_router --vllm-url http://:8000 \ --decode :5556:5557 --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 \ --parser glm47 --port 23333 # 4b) General traffic → native vLLM decode pool, via vLLM's standard NixlConnector # disaggregation proxy, pointing prefill :8000 → native decode :8001. ``` **Note.** Running NIXL end to end (both the native and TileRT connectors in NIXL mode) lets the shared prefill use a single transfer library. Only the prefill's `--kv-transfer-config` differs from Topology A; the TileRT decode node is unchanged, and the native decode instance plus its proxy follow vLLM's usual `NixlConnector` disaggregation setup. ## Status & Future Work TileRT is currently offered as a preview release, and we’re just getting started. We are continuously improving the installation experience and enhancing end-to-end performance. Future releases will keep pushing the boundaries of low-latency generation. Thank you for your interest and support — stay tuned, even faster token generation is on the way!

"""TileRT Python package.

Two backend libraries ship with TileRT — one per model family:

  - ``libtilert_dsv32.so``  (DeepSeek-V3.2)
  - ``libtilert_glm5.so``   (GLM-5)

They are NOT loaded at import time. The caller selects a backend via
``load_backend(model_type)`` (done automatically by ``tilert.generate``).
Only one backend may be loaded per process — both register the ``tilert``
torch-op namespace. Run DSv3.2 and GLM-5 in separate processes.
"""

import ctypes
import logging
import os
from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError
from importlib.metadata import version as pkg_version
from pathlib import Path

import torch

if not hasattr(torch, "ops"):
    raise RuntimeError("PyTorch is required but torch.ops is not available")

try:
    __version__ = pkg_version("tilert")
except PackageNotFoundError:
    __version__ = "0.0.0"


def init_logging() -> logging.Logger:
    """Initialize logging configuration."""
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.DEBUG,
        format="%(filename)s:%(lineno)d [%(levelname)s]: %(message)s",
    )
    return logging.getLogger(__name__)


logger = init_logging()

_BACKENDS = {
    "deepseek_v3_2": "libtilert_dsv32.so",
    "glm5": "libtilert_glm5.so",
}

_loaded_backend: str | None = None


def load_backend(model_type: str) -> None:
    """Load the backend for ``model_type`` (lazy, once per process).

    DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 ship as separate libraries; the matching one is
    loaded on first use. Loading a second, different backend in the same
    process raises (both libraries define the ``tilert`` op namespace).
    """
    global _loaded_backend
    so_name = _BACKENDS.get(model_type)
    if so_name is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown model_type {model_type!r}. Supported: {sorted(_BACKENDS)}")
    if _loaded_backend is not None:
        if _loaded_backend != so_name:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"TileRT backend '{_loaded_backend}' already loaded; cannot load "
                f"'{so_name}' in the same process. Run {model_type} in a fresh process."
            )
        return
    pkg_dir = Path(__file__).parent
    lib_path = pkg_dir / so_name
    if not lib_path.exists():
        fallback = pkg_dir / "libtilert.so"
        if not fallback.exists():
            raise RuntimeError(f"Backend library not found: {lib_path}.")
        lib_path = fallback
    ctypes.CDLL(str(lib_path), mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL | os.RTLD_LAZY)
    torch.ops.load_library(str(lib_path))
    _loaded_backend = so_name
    logger.info(
        "Loaded TileRT backend %s (%s) for model_type=%s", so_name, lib_path.name, model_type
    )


from .tilert_init import tilert_init  # noqa: E402

__all__ = [
    "logger",
    "load_backend",
    "tilert_init",
    "__version__",
]

"""Text generation script for TileRT."""

import time
from argparse import ArgumentParser
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import tilert

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.generator import DSAv32Generator
    from tilert.models.glm_5.generator import GLM5Generator
from tilert.benchmark import BenchMode
from tilert.benchmark import coding_prompt as coding_bench
from tilert.benchmark import long_prompt as long_bench
from tilert.benchmark import merge_stats, print_summary_table
from tilert.benchmark import short_prompt as short_bench
from tilert.benchmark.config import get_weights_dir


def get_generator(
    model_type: str,
    max_new_tokens: int,
    temperature: float,
    model_weights_dir: str,
    with_mtp: bool,
    top_p: float = 0.9,
    top_k: int = 256,
    enable_thinking: bool = False,
    sampling_seed: int = 42,
) -> "DSAv32Generator | GLM5Generator":
    """Load the matching backend .so and build the generator for ``model_type``.

    DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 ship as separate libraries; only one backend loads
    per process. Generators are imported lazily after the backend is loaded.
    """
    tilert.load_backend(model_type)

    if model_type == "deepseek_v3_2":
        from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.generator import DSAv32Generator
        from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.model_args import ModelArgs as DSAv32ModelArgs

        return DSAv32Generator(
            model_args=DSAv32ModelArgs(),
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            temperature=temperature,
            model_weights_dir=model_weights_dir,
            with_mtp=with_mtp,
            top_p=top_p,
            top_k=top_k,
            use_topp=top_p < 1.0,
            sampling_seed=sampling_seed,
            enable_thinking=enable_thinking,
        )

    if model_type == "glm5":
        from tilert.models.glm_5.generator import GLM5Generator
        from tilert.models.glm_5.model_args import ModelArgsGLM5

        return GLM5Generator(
            model_args=ModelArgsGLM5(),
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            temperature=temperature,
            model_weights_dir=model_weights_dir,
            with_mtp=with_mtp,
            top_p=top_p,
            top_k=top_k,
            use_topp=top_p < 1.0,
            enable_thinking=enable_thinking,
            sampling_seed=sampling_seed,
        )

    raise ValueError(f"unsupported model_type: {model_type!r}")


def parse_args():  # type: ignore
    parser = ArgumentParser(description="Command-line interface for text generation.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model-weights-dir",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Path to model weights directory (resolved from ~/.tilert/config.toml if omitted)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model",
        type=str,
        default="deepseek_v3_2",
        choices=["deepseek_v3_2", "glm5"],
        help="Model type to use (default: deepseek_v3_2).",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--max-new-tokens", type=int, default=4000, help="Max tokens to generate")
    parser.add_argument("--temperature", type=float, default=1.0, help="Sampling temperature")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--top-p",
        type=float,
        default=1.0,
        help="Top-p (nucleus) sampling threshold. Use < 1.0 to enable top-p sampling (e.g. 0.9)",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=256, help="Top-k sampling threshold")
    parser.add_argument("--interactive", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--with-mtp",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) for speculative decoding",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--use-random-weights",
        action="store_true",
        help="Use random weights instead of pretrained (for testing MTP without real weights)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--enable-thinking",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable thinking mode in chat template",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--sampling-seed",
        type=int,
        default=42,
        help="Sampling seed for top-p sampling (fixed per request, default: 42)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model-name",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Override display name for benchmark tables",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--tag",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Tag for regression_plots/ directory (default: auto-detect from git state)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--modes",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Comma-separated mode filters: top-k1,top-p0.95 (default: all)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--workloads",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Comma-separated workload filters: short,coding,long (default: all)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--enable-logprobs",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable kernel-level top-256 logprobs export (for benchmarking overhead)",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    """
    Usage (run as a module; --model-weights-dir may be omitted if the path is
    registered under ~/.tilert/config.toml). Run DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 in
    separate processes — the two backends cannot coexist in one interpreter.

    # DeepSeek-V3.2 — standard generation with pretrained weights:
    python -m tilert.generate --model deepseek_v3_2 \
        --model-weights-dir /path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT \
        --max-new-tokens 1000 2>&1 | tee test.log

    # DeepSeek-V3.2 — MTP generation with random weights (for testing):
    python -m tilert.generate --model deepseek_v3_2 --with-mtp --use-random-weights \
        --model-weights-dir /path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT \
        --max-new-tokens 1000 2>&1 | tee test.log

    # DeepSeek-V3.2 — MTP generation with pretrained weights:
    python -m tilert.generate --model deepseek_v3_2 --with-mtp \
        --model-weights-dir /path/to/DeepSeek-V3.2-TileRT \
        --max-new-tokens 1000 2>&1 | tee test.log

    # GLM-5 — standard generation:
    python -m tilert.generate --model glm5 \
        --model-weights-dir /path/to/GLM-5-FP8-TileRT \
        --max-new-tokens 1000 2>&1 | tee test.log

    # GLM-5 — MTP generation:
    python -m tilert.generate --model glm5 --with-mtp \
        --model-weights-dir /path/to/GLM-5-FP8-TileRT \
        --max-new-tokens 1000 2>&1 | tee test.log
    """
    args = parse_args()

    config_key = args.model
    model_name = args.model.upper()
    if args.model_name:
        model_name = args.model_name
    model_weights_dir = get_weights_dir(config_key, cli_override=args.model_weights_dir)

    if args.interactive:
        with_mtp = args.with_mtp
    else:
        with_mtp = True

    generator = get_generator(
        model_type=args.model,
        max_new_tokens=args.max_new_tokens,
        temperature=args.temperature,
        model_weights_dir=model_weights_dir,
        with_mtp=with_mtp,
        top_p=args.top_p,
        top_k=args.top_k,
        enable_thinking=args.enable_thinking,
        sampling_seed=args.sampling_seed,
    )

    t0 = time.monotonic()
    if args.use_random_weights:
        print("Initializing random weights...")
        if hasattr(generator, "init"):
            generator.init()  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        generator.init_random_weights()
    else:
        print("Loading pretrained weights...")
        generator.from_pretrained()
    load_time = time.monotonic() - t0

    if args.enable_logprobs:
        if hasattr(generator.decode_layer, "set_logprobs_enabled"):
            generator.decode_layer.set_logprobs_enabled(True)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            print("Logprobs export enabled (top-256)")
        else:
            print(f"Warning: logprobs not supported for {type(generator).__name__}")

    if args.interactive:
        print("Welcome to the TileRT interactive mode! Type '/exit' to exit.")
        while True:
            prompt = input(">>> ")
            if prompt == "/exit":
                break
            _ = generator.generate(prompt)  # type: ignore[has-type]
    else:

        bench_top_p = args.top_p if args.top_p < 1.0 else 0.95
        modes = [
            BenchMode(with_mtp=False, label="top-k1 w/o MTP"),
            BenchMode(with_mtp=True, label="top-k1 w/ MTP"),
            BenchMode(
                with_mtp=True,
                label=f"top-p{bench_top_p} w/ MTP",
                use_topp=True,
                top_p=bench_top_p,
                top_k=args.top_k,
                temperature=args.temperature,
            ),
        ]

        if args.modes:
            allowed = {m.strip() for m in args.modes.split(",")}
            modes = [m for m in modes if any(a in m.label for a in allowed)]
            if not modes:
                raise SystemExit(
                    f"Error: --modes '{args.modes}' matched no benchmark modes. "
                    f"Valid tokens: top-k1, top-p0.95"
                )

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        workload_runners = []
        allowed_workloads = (
            {w.strip() for w in args.workloads.split(",")}
            if args.workloads
            else {"short", "coding", "long"}
        )
        if "short" in allowed_workloads:
            workload_runners.append(short_bench.run)
        if "coding" in allowed_workloads:
            workload_runners.append(coding_bench.run)
        if "long" in allowed_workloads:
            workload_runners.append(long_bench.run)
        if not workload_runners:
            raise SystemExit(
                f"Error: --workloads '{args.workloads}' matched no workloads. "
                f"Valid values: short, coding, long"
            )

        all_bench_results = [
            runner(generator, modes) for runner in workload_runners  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        ]
        bench_time = time.monotonic() - t0
        all_bench_stats = [stats for stats, _ in all_bench_results]

        print_summary_table(
            merge_stats(all_bench_stats),
            model_name=model_name,
        )

        total = load_time + bench_time
        print(f"\n## {model_name} Timing")
        print()
        print("| Phase | Time |")
        print("|-------|------|")
        print(f"| Loading | {load_time:.1f}s |")
        print(f"| Benchmark | {bench_time:.1f}s |")
        print(f"| **Total** | **{total:.1f}s** |")

    print("Cleaning up...")
    generator.cleanup()

"""Tilert init operation module."""

import torch

__all__ = [
    "tilert_init",
    "tilert_force_init",
]


def tilert_init() -> None:
    """Tilert init operation."""
    torch.ops.tilert.tilert_init_op()


def tilert_force_init() -> None:
    """Tilert force init operation."""
    torch.ops.tilert.tilert_force_init_op()

[project]
name = "tilert"
dynamic = ["version"]

description = "TileRT"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = {text = "MIT"}
authors = [{name = "TileRT-team", email = "contact@tilert.ai"}]
classifiers = [
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
]

dependencies = [
    # Pinned to the exact ABI the v0.1.5 wheel was built against. ``torch`` must
    # come from PyTorch's cu130 index (``--index-url
    # https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130``); installing from PyPI yields a
    # CUDA build that does not match the cu130-linked tilert binary.
    "torch==2.11.0",
    "transformers==4.46.3",
    "tokenizers==0.20.3",
    "numpy",
    "scipy",
    "einops",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=7.0.0",
    "black==25.1.0",
    "flake8==7.1.2",
    "flake8-bugbear==24.12.12",
    "flake8-comprehensions==3.16.0",
    "flake8-docstrings==1.7.0",
    "flake8-simplify==0.21.0",
    "flake8-unused-arguments==0.0.13",
    "flake8-variables-names==0.0.6",
    "flake8-return==1.2.0",
    "flake8-print==5.0.0",
    "isort==6.0.1",
    "mypy==1.15.0",
    "bandit==1.8.3",
    "pyupgrade==3.19.1",
    "commitizen==4.4.1",

1	"""Base classes for deepseek v3."""
2	
3	import os
4	from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
5	from enum import Enum
6	from typing import Any, ClassVar
7	
8	import torch
9	import torch.nn as nn
10	
11	from tilert import logger
12	from tilert.models.deepseek_config import get_rank, get_world_size
13	from tilert.models.deepseek_v3_2.model_args import ModelArgs
14	from tilert.utils import get_profile_log_tensor
15	
16	__all__ = [
17	    "TileRTModule",
18	]
19	
20	ModelArgsLike = Any
21	
22	
23	class TilertWeightsConverter:
24	    """Tilert weights converter"""
25	
26	    def __init__(self, model_args: ModelArgsLike, num_devices: int):
27	        self.model_args = model_args
28	        self.num_devices = num_devices
29	
30	    def dispatch(self, algorithm: Enum, weights: list[torch.Tensor]) -> Any:
31	        dispatch_method = getattr(self, f"convert_to_{algorithm.value}")
32	        return dispatch_method(weights)
33	
34	
35	class TileRTModule(nn.Module, ABC):
36	    """Base class for all TileRT modules.
37	
38	    This class serves as an abstract base for implementing TileRT modules.
39	    All module classes should inherit from this class and implement their
40	    own forward method.
41	    """
42	
43	    _SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS: ClassVar[dict[str, list[Enum]]] = {}
44	    _VALID_COMPUTE_KERNEL_TYPES: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset(
45	        {
46	            "bf16",
47	            "fp8",
48	            "fp8mma",
49	            "general",
50	            "bf16mma",
51	            "fp16mma",
52	            "fp8mma_68cta",
53	        }
54	    )
55	
56	    @classmethod
57	    def get_supported_algorithms(cls, arch_name: str) -> list[Enum]:
58	        """Return supported algorithms for the given architecture."""
59	        if arch_name not in cls._SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS:
60	            raise ValueError(
61	                f"{cls.__name__} does not support arch '{arch_name}'. "
62	                f"Supported: {list(cls._SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS.keys())}"
63	            )
64	        return cls._SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS[arch_name]
65	
66	    def __init__(
67	        self,
68	        op_name: str = "",
69	        golden_weights_dir: str = "",
70	        tilert_weights_dir: str = "",
71	        layer_idx: int = 0,
72	        compute_kernel_type: str = "bf16",
73	        model_args: ModelArgsLike | None = None,
74	        num_devices: int = 8,
75	        device_id: int = 0,
76	        *args: Any,
77	        **kwargs: Any,
78	    ) -> None:
79	        """Initialize the operation.
80	
81	        Args:
82	            op_name: Optional operation name. Defaults to class name.
83	            golden_weights_dir: Optional path to golden weights directory.
84	            tilert_weights_path: Optional path to tilert weights directory.
85	            layer_idx: Layer index.
86	            compute_kernel_type: Compute kernel type, bf16 by default; fp8 is also supported.
87	            *args: Additional positional arguments.
88	            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments.
89	        """
90	        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
91	
92	        self.model_args: ModelArgsLike = model_args if model_args is not None else ModelArgs()
93	        self.num_devices = num_devices
94	        self.device_id = device_id
95	        self.algorithm: Enum | None = None
96	
97	        self.is_var_init = False
98	        self.is_tilert_weights_init = False
99	        self.is_ref_weights_init = False
100	
101	        self.profile_logs: torch.Tensor | None = None
102	
103	        self.layer_idx = layer_idx
104	
105	        self.flag_enable_tilert = False
106	
107	        if compute_kernel_type not in self._VALID_COMPUTE_KERNEL_TYPES:
108	            raise ValueError(
109	                f"Invalid compute kernel type: {compute_kernel_type}, "
110	                f"must be one of {sorted(self._VALID_COMPUTE_KERNEL_TYPES)}."
111	            )
112	        self.compute_kernel_type = compute_kernel_type
113	
114	        self.flag_enable_profiling_log = False
115	        self.flag_enable_external_profiling_log = False
116	
117	        self.op_name = type(self).__name__ if op_name == "" else op_name
118	        self.profile_log_dir = "profile_logs"
119	
120	        self.golden_weights_dir = golden_weights_dir
121	        self.tilert_weights_dir = tilert_weights_dir
122	
123	        self.profile_logs = get_profile_log_tensor()
124	
125	    def get_cache_vars(self) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
126	        return []
127	
128	    def get_tilert_weights_alias(self) -> list[str]:
129	        return list(self.tilert_weights_alias())
130	
131	    def get_ref_weights_alias(self) -> list[str]:
132	        return list(self.ref_weights_alias())
133	
134	    def set_algorithm(self, algorithm: Enum) -> None:
135	        """Set the algorithm for the module.
136	
137	        Args:
138	            algorithm: Algorithm.
139	        """
140	        if self._SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS:
141	            arch = self.model_args.arch_name
142	            supported = self.get_supported_algorithms(arch)
143	            if algorithm not in supported:
144	                raise ValueError(
145	                    f"{type(self).__name__}: algorithm {algorithm} not supported "
146	                    f"for arch '{arch}'. Supported: {supported}"
147	                )
148	        self.algorithm = algorithm
149	
150	    def register_weights(self, weights_config: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
151	        """Register weights configuration.
152	
153	        Args:
154	            weights_config: Dictionary mapping weight names to their configurations.
155	        """
156	        self.weight_loader.register_weights(weights_config)
157	
158	    def get_profile_log_path(self) -> str:
159	        """Get the path to the profile log file.
160	
161	        Returns:
162	            Path to the profile log file.
163	        """
164	        return os.path.join(self.profile_log_dir, f"{self.op_name}.xlsx")
165	
166	    def get_external_profile_log_path(self) -> str:
167	        """Get the path to the external profile log file.
168	
169	        Returns:
170	            Path to the external profile log file.
171	        """
172	        return os.path.join(self.profile_log_dir, f"{self.op_name}.json")
173	
174	    def world_size(self) -> int:
175	        """Get the world size.
176	
177	        Returns:
178	            World size.
179	        """
180	        return int(get_world_size())
181	
182	    def rank(self) -> int:
183	        """Get the rank.
184	
185	        Returns:
186	            Rank.
187	        """
188	        return int(get_rank())
189	
190	    @abstractmethod
191	    def golden_forward(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
192	        """Golden forward pass.
193	
194	        Args:
195	            *args: Variable length argument list.
196	            **kwargs: Arbitrary keyword arguments.
197	
198	        Raises:
199	            NotImplementedError: This method must be implemented by subclasses.
200	        """
201	        del args, kwargs
202	        raise NotImplementedError("Golden forward not implemented")
203	
204	    @abstractmethod
205	    def tilert_forward(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:  # noqa: U100
206	        """Tilert forward method to be implemented by subclasses.
207	
208	        Args:
209	            *args: Variable length argument list.
210	            **kwargs: Arbitrary keyword arguments.
211	        """
212	        del args, kwargs
213	        raise NotImplementedError("Tilert forward not implemented")
214	
215	    def enable_profiling_log(self, enable: bool = True) -> None:
216	        """Enable profiling log for this module and all submodules.
217	
218	        Args:
219	            enable: Whether to enable profiling.
220	        """
221	        for module in self.modules():
222	            if isinstance(module, TileRTModule):
223	                logger.info(f"Enable profiling for {module.__class__.__name__}")
224	                module.flag_enable_profiling_log = enable
225	
226	    def enable_external_profiling_log(self, enable: bool = True) -> None:
227	        """Enable external profiling log for this module and all submodules.
228	
229	        Args:
230	            enable: Whether to enable external profiling.
231	        """
232	        for module in self.modules():
233	            if isinstance(module, TileRTModule):
234	                logger.info(f"Enable external profiling for {module.__class__.__name__}")
235	                module.flag_enable_external_profiling_log = enable
236	
237	    def enable_tilert(self, enable: bool = True) -> None:  # type: ignore
238	        for module in self.modules():
239	            if isinstance(module, TileRTModule):
240	                logger.info(f"Enable tilert for {module.__class__.__name__}")
241	                module.flag_enable_tilert = enable
242	                if enable:
243	                    module.to_tilert_weights()
244	
245	
246	class SerializableTileRTModule(TileRTModule):
247	    """Serializable TileRT module."""
248	
249	    def __init__(
250	        self,
251	        model_args: ModelArgsLike,
252	        device_id: int,
253	        num_devices: int,
254	        remove_selected: bool = False,
255	    ):
256	        super().__init__(
257	            type(self).__name__, model_args=model_args, device_id=device_id, num_devices=num_devices
258	        )
259	        self.remove_selected = remove_selected
260	
261	        self.exec_seq: list[TileRTModule] = []
262	        self.prefix_seq: list[str] = []
263	        self.suffix_seq: list[str] = []
264	        self.retain_weights_seq: list[bool] = []
265	
266	    def get_cache_vars(self) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
267	        cache_vars = []
268	        for op in self.exec_seq:
269	            cache_vars.extend(op.get_cache_vars())
270	        return cache_vars
271	
272	    def register_op(
273	        self, op: TileRTModule, prefix: str = "", suffix: str = "", retain_weights: bool = False
274	    ) -> None:
275	        self.exec_seq.append(op)
276	        self.prefix_seq.append(prefix)
277	        self.suffix_seq.append(suffix)
278	        self.retain_weights_seq.append(retain_weights)
279	
280	    def get_tilert_weights_alias(self) -> list[str]:
281	        weights_alias: list[str] = []
282	        for op in self.exec_seq:
283	            weights_alias.extend(op.get_tilert_weights_alias())
284	        return weights_alias
285	
286	    def get_ref_weights_alias(self) -> list[str]:
287	        weights_alias: list[str] = []
288	        for op in self.exec_seq:
289	            weights_alias.extend(op.get_ref_weights_alias())
290	        return weights_alias
291	
292	    def get_weights_list(self) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
293	        weights = []
294	        for op in self.exec_seq:
295	            weights.extend(op.get_weights_list())
296	        return weights
297	
298	    def device_sharding(self, raw_weights_map: dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
299	        sharded_weights_map: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
300	        for op in self.exec_seq:
301	            sharded_weights_map.update(op.device_sharding(raw_weights_map))
302	        return sharded_weights_map
303	
304	    @property
305	    def tilert_tensor_alias(self) -> list[str]:
306	        """Return tilert tensor alias of the first sub-op (RMSNormProjxWqkvia)."""
307	        tensor_alias: list[str] = []
308	        for op in self.exec_seq:
309	            tensor_alias.extend(op.tilert_weights_alias())
310	        return tensor_alias
311	
312	    @property
313	    def ref_tensor_alias(self) -> list[str]:
314	        """Return reference tensor alias of the first sub-op (RMSNormProjxWqkvia)."""
315	        tensor_alias: list[str] = []
316	        for op in self.exec_seq:
317	            tensor_alias.extend(op.ref_weights_alias())
318	        return tensor_alias

322	            self.exec_seq, self.prefix_seq, self.suffix_seq, self.retain_weights_seq
323	        ):
324	            if op.is_tilert_weights_init:
325	                logger.debug(f"Skipping init_tilert_weights for {op.op_name} (already initialized)")

21	def stats_time(time_list: list[float], title: str) -> None:
22	    if len(time_list) > 0:
23	        avg_time = sum(time_list) / len(time_list)
24	        std_dev = math.sqrt(sum((x - avg_time) ** 2 for x in time_list) / len(time_list))

28	        logger.info(f"--Effective tokens per second: {1 / avg_time:.4f}")

154	    @torch.inference_mode()
155	    def generate(
156	        self,
157	        prompt: str,
158	        print_log: bool = True,
159	        with_mtp: bool | None = None,
160	        prompt_tokens: list[int] | None = None,
161	    ) -> tuple[str, list[float], list[int], int]:
162	        """Main function to load the model and perform single sequence generation.
163	
164	        Args:
165	            prompt: The input prompt string.
166	            print_log: Whether to print generation logs.
167	            with_mtp: Override MTP mode for this call. None uses self.with_mtp.
168	                Requires MTP weights to have been loaded (self.with_mtp=True).
169	            prompt_tokens: Pre-tokenized prompt tokens. If provided, skip tokenization
170	                and use these tokens directly (useful for exact-length benchmarking).
171	
172	        Returns:
173	            Tuple of (result_text, time_list, accepted_counts, prompt_len).
174	            accepted_counts is empty for non-MTP mode.
175	        """
176	        active_mtp = with_mtp if with_mtp is not None else self.with_mtp
177	        if active_mtp and not self.with_mtp:
178	            raise ValueError("Cannot use MTP mode: MTP weights were not loaded")
179	        self.decode_layer.set_sampling_seed(self.sampling_seed, with_mtp=active_mtp)
180	        if active_mtp:
181	            return self._generate_with_mtp(prompt, print_log, prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens)
182	        result, time_list, prompt_len = self._generate_without_mtp(
183	            prompt, print_log, with_mtp=active_mtp, prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens
184	        )
185	        return result, time_list, [], prompt_len
186	
187	    def _generate_without_mtp(
188	        self,
189	        prompt: str,
190	        print_log: bool = True,
191	        with_mtp: bool = False,
192	        prompt_tokens: list[int] | None = None,
193	    ) -> tuple[str, list[float], int]:
194	        """Standard generation without MTP."""
195	        if prompt_tokens is None:
196	            prompt_tokens = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
197	                [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
198	                add_generation_prompt=True,
199	                thinking=self.enable_thinking,
200	            )
201	
202	        max_seq_len = self.config.max_seq_len
203	        prompt_len = len(prompt_tokens)
204	        total_len = min(max_seq_len, self.max_new_tokens + prompt_len)
205	
206	        tokens = torch.full(
207	            (self.batch_size, total_len), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=self.default_device
208	        )
209	        tokens[0, :prompt_len] = torch.tensor(
210	            prompt_tokens, dtype=torch.long, device=self.default_device
211	        )
212	        prompt_mask = tokens != -1
213	
214	        prev_pos = 0
215	        finished = torch.tensor(
216	            [False] * self.batch_size, dtype=torch.bool, device=self.default_device
217	        )
218	
219	        time_list = []
220	        for cur_pos_val in range(1, total_len):
221	            start_time = time.time()
222	            multi_devices_results = self.decode_layer.forward(
223	                tokens[0, prev_pos], with_mtp=with_mtp
224	            )
225	            end_time = time.time()
226	            time_list.append(end_time - start_time)
227	
228	            intermediates, *_ = multi_devices_results[0]
229	            next_token = intermediates[Idx.TOKEN_OUT][0][0]
230	
231	            next_token = torch.where(
232	                prompt_mask[0, cur_pos_val], tokens[0, cur_pos_val], next_token
233	            )
234	            tokens[0, cur_pos_val] = next_token
235	            finished |= torch.logical_and(~prompt_mask[0, cur_pos_val], next_token == self.eos_id)
236	            prev_pos = cur_pos_val
237	            if cur_pos_val >= prompt_len:
238	                decoded_tokens = self.tokenizer.decode(
239	                    [next_token.item()], skip_special_tokens=True
240	                )
241	                if print_log:
242	                    print(decoded_tokens, end="", flush=True)
243	
244	            if finished.all():
245	                break
246	
247	        if print_log:
248	            print("\n")
249	            logger.info(f"--Number of tokens generated: {len(time_list)}")
250	
251	            stats_time(time_list, "==== Performance ====")
252	            print("\n")
253	
254	        self.decode_layer.reset_sequence()
255	
256	        completion_tokens = []
257	        for _, toks in enumerate(tokens.tolist()):
258	            toks = toks[prompt_len : prompt_len + self.max_new_tokens]
259	            if self.eos_id in toks:
260	                toks = toks[: toks.index(self.eos_id)]
261	            completion_tokens.append(toks)
262	
263	        decoded_tokens = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(completion_tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)
264	
265	        return f"{decoded_tokens[0]}\n" if decoded_tokens else "", time_list, prompt_len
266	
267	    def _generate_with_mtp(
268	        self,
269	        prompt: str,
270	        print_log: bool = True,
271	        prompt_tokens: list[int] | None = None,
272	    ) -> tuple[str, list[float], list[int], int]:
273	        """Generation with MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculative decoding."""
274	        if prompt_tokens is None:
275	            prompt_tokens = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
276	                [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
277	                add_generation_prompt=True,
278	                thinking=self.enable_thinking,
279	            )
280	
281	        max_seq_len = self.config.max_seq_len
282	        prompt_len = len(prompt_tokens)
283	        total_len = min(max_seq_len, self.max_new_tokens + prompt_len)
284	
285	        tokens = torch.full(
286	            (self.batch_size, total_len), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=self.default_device
287	        )
288	        tokens[0, :prompt_len] = torch.tensor(
289	            prompt_tokens, dtype=torch.long, device=self.default_device
290	        )
291	
292	        prefill_time_list = []
293	        decode_time_list = []
294	        decode_accepted_counts = []
295	        cur_pos = 0
296	
297	        while cur_pos < prompt_len - 1:
298	            draft_end = min(cur_pos + self.mtp_seq_len, prompt_len)
299	            draft_tokens = tokens[0, cur_pos:draft_end].clone()
300	            actual_token_count = draft_tokens.shape[0]
301	
302	            if actual_token_count < self.mtp_seq_len:
303	                pad_token = draft_tokens[-1].item()
304	                padding = torch.full(
305	                    (self.mtp_seq_len - actual_token_count,),
306	                    pad_token,
307	                    dtype=torch.long,
308	                    device=self.default_device,
309	                )
310	                draft_tokens = torch.cat([draft_tokens, padding])
311	
312	            draft_tokens = draft_tokens.reshape(1, self.mtp_seq_len).to(torch.int32)
313	
314	            mtp_extra_pos = cur_pos + self.mtp_seq_len
315	            if mtp_extra_pos < prompt_len:
316	                mtp_extra_token = int(tokens[0, mtp_extra_pos].item())
317	            else:
318	                mtp_extra_token = int(tokens[0, draft_end - 1].item())
319	            self.decode_layer.set_prefill_mtp_extra_token(mtp_extra_token)
320	
321	            self.decode_layer.set_prefill_valid_tokens(actual_token_count)
322	
323	            start_time = time.time()
324	            self.decode_layer.forward(draft_tokens, with_mtp=True)
325	            end_time = time.time()
326	            prefill_time_list.append(end_time - start_time)
327	
328	            cur_pos += actual_token_count
329	
330	        cur_pos = prompt_len - 1
331	        self.set_cur_pos(prompt_len - 1)
332	
333	        self.decode_layer.set_prefill_valid_tokens(0)
334	
335	        finished = False
336	        while cur_pos < total_len - 1 and not finished:
337	            if cur_pos == prompt_len - 1:
338	                last_token = tokens[0, prompt_len - 1].item()
339	                draft_tokens = torch.full(
340	                    (self.mtp_seq_len,),
341	                    last_token,
342	                    dtype=torch.long,
343	                    device=self.default_device,
344	                )
345	                draft_tokens = draft_tokens.reshape(1, self.mtp_seq_len).to(torch.int32)
346	            else:
347	                draft_tokens = self.decode_layer.get_next_draft_tokens(0).reshape(
348	                    1, self.mtp_seq_len
349	                )
350	
351	            start_time = time.time()
352	            self.decode_layer.forward(draft_tokens, with_mtp=True)
353	            end_time = time.time()
354	            decode_time_list.append(end_time - start_time)
355	
356	            num_accepted = self.decode_layer.get_num_accepted(0)
357	            predicted_tokens = self.decode_layer.get_predicted_tokens(0).flatten()
358	            decode_accepted_counts.append(num_accepted)
359	
360	            num_output_tokens = num_accepted
361	            for i in range(num_output_tokens):
362	                if cur_pos + 1 + i >= total_len:
363	                    break
364	                new_token = int(predicted_tokens[i].item())
365	                tokens[0, cur_pos + 1 + i] = new_token
366	
367	                if cur_pos + 1 + i >= prompt_len and print_log:
368	                    decoded_text = self.tokenizer.decode([new_token], skip_special_tokens=True)
369	                    print(decoded_text, end="", flush=True)
370	
371	                if new_token == self.eos_id:
372	                    finished = True
373	                    break
374	
375	            cur_pos += num_accepted
376	
377	        if print_log:
378	            print("\n")
379	            total_tokens = sum(decode_accepted_counts)
380	            logger.info(f"--Number of forward calls (decode): {len(decode_accepted_counts)}")
381	            logger.info(f"--Total tokens generated: {total_tokens}")
382	            if len(decode_accepted_counts) > 0:
383	                avg_accepted = sum(decode_accepted_counts) / len(decode_accepted_counts)
384	                min_accepted = min(decode_accepted_counts)
385	                max_accepted = max(decode_accepted_counts)
386	                logger.info(
387	                    f"--Accepted tokens per call: mean={avg_accepted:.2f}, "
388	                    f"min={min_accepted}, max={max_accepted}"
389	                )
390	
391	            if decode_time_list:
392	                total_decode_time = sum(decode_time_list)
393	                effective_tps = total_tokens / total_decode_time if total_decode_time > 0 else 0
394	                avg_time_ms = total_decode_time / len(decode_time_list) * 1000
395	                logger.info(f"--Avg forward time: {avg_time_ms:.2f}ms")
396	                logger.info(f"--Effective TPS (with MTP): {effective_tps:.2f} tokens/s")
397	
398	            print("\n")
399	
400	        self.decode_layer.reset_sequence()
401	
402	        completion_tokens = []
403	        for _, toks in enumerate(tokens.tolist()):
404	            toks = toks[prompt_len : prompt_len + self.max_new_tokens]
405	            toks = [t for t in toks if t != -1]
406	            if self.eos_id in toks:
407	                toks = toks[: toks.index(self.eos_id)]
408	            completion_tokens.append(toks)
409	
410	        decoded_tokens = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(completion_tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)
411	
412	        return (
413	            f"{decoded_tokens[0]}\n" if decoded_tokens else "",
414	            decode_time_list,
415	            decode_accepted_counts,
416	            prompt_len,
417	        )
